title: Yusuf asks for work
body: Yusuf is a careful young trader. He has no house of his own. He asks you to hire him and send him out with ten loads of your linen.

choices.label: Hire Yusuf and send him
choices.hint: The clerk's fee is 4 dinars. The next sheet shows what sending him costs.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.hint: Without an agent you cannot send anyone out. Partners like a house that waits.

note: Traders in the Geniza papers spread their risk. They took part in many small partnerships instead of one large one.

sources.at: introduction, pp. 22 to 23; spreading risk by many small partnerships

from.name: Ali, a young trader of Cairo

title: Ali asks for work
body: Ali is bold and quick. He has travelled before and knows the south. He has no house of his own, and he asks you to take him on. Another agent means another set of goods out at once. It also means another wage.

choices.label: Hire Ali
choices.hint: The clerk's fee is 4 dinars. Your other agents hear that you hire people, and think better of you in three seasons. The Outfit button on the map shows what sending him costs.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.hint: You save the fee. Partners like a house that waits, and say so in two seasons.

note: A merchant of the Geniza papers did not always pay a travelling manager a wage. Sometimes he paid the manager's living costs on the road instead.

sources.at: pp. 322, 325 to 326; a travelling manager had his living expenses paid instead of a wage

from.name: Samir, a young man of Cairo

title: Samir wants a qirad
body: Samir has no money, but he wants to carry goods for you. He offers a qirad, a deal where you pay for the goods and he keeps a share of the profit. Or you can pay him a plain wage.

choices.label: Agree to a qirad
choices.hint: He keeps a third of the profit. You carry any loss. Some partners think Samir is too young, then come round. The next sheet shows the cost.

choices.label: Pay him a wage
choices.hint: You keep all the profit. He is paid even if the goods are lost. Some partners think Samir is too young. The next sheet shows the cost.

choices.label: Not now
choices.hint: Some partners think Samir is too young.

note: Merchants had long made deals like this. The partner with the money bore any loss, and the traveller lost only his work.

sources.at: p. 317; the worker's smaller share and no share in the loss
the rules of the qirad from the law books

title: Yusuf asks to go further
body: Yusuf is on the road to {to}. He sends word by a traveller. He asks to go on past {to} if the price is better there. He says he may do better, and he will keep to your plan if you say so.

choices.label: Let him go further if the price is better
choices.hint: He may do better. A longer road costs 4 dinars now, and you carry the risk. He trusts you more in three seasons.

choices.label: Keep him to {to}
choices.hint: Yusuf will keep his word, and partners like a house that holds its orders.

note: Contracts had long said where an agent could trade. In the Geniza papers an agent who went beyond those limits and lost something paid the whole loss himself.

sources.at: p. 327; a manager who broke the contract's terms paid the whole loss

title: Mariam names her terms
body: Mariam is a Coptic Christian trader. She is careful, and her word is good. She has heard how your house treats its people. She asks to carry your goods, and she offers two ways to pay her.

choices.label: Give her a third of the profit
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars in four seasons. She carries the risk of her work, and you the loss.

choices.label: Pay her a plain wage
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. She is paid even if the goods are lost.

choices.label: Ask her to come back later
choices.hint: She will wait a little, and you gain 3 dinars in two seasons.

note: In the usual Geniza contract a traveller who was paid a share of the profit did not share in any loss. A few contracts did make him share it.

sources.at: pp. 317 and 325; the worker's share, normally one third, and no loss for him; the rarer contract that made the manager share the loss

title: Matteo wants one job
body: Matteo is a trader from Genoa who is in Cairo for the season. He drives a hard bargain. He asks to work for your house for a fee of his own. After that he may take more work from you.

choices.label: Pay him a fee for the one job
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars. He stays free to go.

choices.label: Hire him on a plain wage
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars. He is paid whatever happens.

choices.label: Ask him to bring a letter from someone you know
choices.hint: He will come back, or he will not. If he does, 3 dinars come in three seasons.

note: In the Geniza papers an agent who did a special job was paid a commission, a fee for that job alone. It was not a payment for the friendship.

sources.at: p. 316; the commission paid for a special service

title: Camels for the desert
body: Fuad owns camels in Qus. Goods go from Qus over the desert to the port of Aydhab. He asks five dinars to carry about 800 pounds of your goods on two camels.

choices.label: Hire two camels and add a thank-you
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now and 1 more in two seasons, a thank-you when the goods arrive safely. Fuad speaks well of you.

choices.label: Hire two camels, nothing more
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. Fuad is paid and no more.

choices.label: Say you will hire next year
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Fuad finds another customer.

note: In a lawsuit of 1097, a merchant hired two camels for about 800 pounds of goods from Qus to Aydhab. He paid five dinars, and a third more when the goods arrived safely.

title: Food for seventy nights
body: Idris plans a road from Takadda to Tuat. No grain is found between the two towns. Only meat, curdled milk and butter can be bought, and they are bought with cloth. He asks how much food to carry.

choices.label: Buy food for seventy nights
choices.hint: It costs 9 dinars now. Nobody goes hungry, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Buy less and trust to luck
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. If the road runs long, your people go hungry.

choices.label: Hire a guide who knows the road
choices.hint: It costs 7 dinars now. The guide knows where food can be found, and foreign houses hear of it.

note: In 1353 Ibn Battuta bought food for seventy nights on the road from Takadda to Tuat, where no grain is found. This is later evidence, after the game's years.

title: Fourteen days without water
body: Yunus is a guide at Tuat. He says the road to Walata has fourteen days with no water. Only camels used to thirst can cross it. He offers to lead your caravan.

choices.label: Hire him and carry water
choices.hint: It costs 9 dinars now. The caravan crosses, and partners think well of you.

choices.label: Try another road
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. The way is longer, but foreign houses hear of your care.

choices.label: Do not cross the desert
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Yunus finds another customer.

note: Al-Umari wrote, from older accounts, that beyond Tabalbalet, the last town, lay fourteen days of desert with no water before Walata. Only camels used to thirst could cross.

title: A runner goes ahead
body: Yahya leads a caravan over the Sahara to Walata. Caravans there send a man ahead with letters, so that friends rent houses and bring water to meet them. Yahya asks if you will pay for a runner.

choices.label: Hire a runner to go ahead
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. Houses and water are ready, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Ask a friend in town to send word
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now. It is cheaper, but the friend may be slow.

choices.label: Go without a runner
choices.hint: It costs nothing. If no one comes to meet the caravan, your people suffer.

note: Caravans hired a man of the Massufa to go ahead to Walata with letters. Ibn Battuta wrote in 1352, after the game's years, that if the messenger died, most of the caravan died too.

from.name: An officer of the pilgrim caravan

title: Guides for the king of Mali
body: The party of Mansa Musa leaves Cairo for Mecca soon. The desert road is hard, and the party needs guides who know the way. Your house is asked to pay part of the guides' fee.

choices.label: Pay part of the guides' fee
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. The court hears that your house helped.

choices.label: Send water skins instead
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. Foreign houses hear of your gift.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The officer remembers.

note: A guide named Mehna son of Abd al-Baqi went with Mansa Musa's party on the pilgrimage in 1324. He told al-Umari that the king gave him 200 mithqals of gold.

title: A broker offers to sell
body: A broker at Pera offers to sell your goods. A broker is a go-between who finds buyers. He takes a fee from each side.

choices.label: Hire him at his rate
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. The sale is steady, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Hire a cheaper broker
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now. The cheaper man sells badly, and word gets round.

choices.label: Sell the goods yourself
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The sale is slow, and foreign houses wonder.

note: At Constantinople a broker took 4 carats, each a twenty-fourth of a perper, from each side for every 100 perpers. Pegolotti says merchants often paid more.

title: Silver into gold, if it pays
body: A Venetian house sends silver to Famagusta. It wants it turned into gold for its galleys, but only if the profit is 8 in 100 or more. It asks you to take the post.

choices.label: Take the post
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. If the profit is too small, you lose your fee, and foreign houses hear of the work.

choices.label: Take it as a loan from the house
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The house lends you its trust, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The house finds another agent.

note: In 1343 Francesco Querini sent silver to Famagusta. His agent was to buy gold if the profit was 8 in 100 or more, and if not, cotton or spices.

title: An interpreter for the long road
body: A merchant bound far east asks you to name a guide who speaks the languages of the road. A good interpreter is dear, and a poor one is cheap.

choices.label: Send an expensive interpreter
choices.hint: It costs 10 dinars now. The road is safer, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Send a cheap one
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. The road is riskier, and word gets round.

choices.label: Send two servants who speak the local tongue
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. They know the road, and foreign houses hear of it.

note: Pegolotti told merchants bound for China to hire a good interpreter at Tana. A company of sixty, he said, was as safe as at home.
